steps.context: Only a gene-level TPM table from Salmon was delivered — no raw counts, no quantification directories. Benjamini-Hochberg for multiple testing; report FDR, not raw p, as the decision statistic

steps.description: Using the filtered normalized log2(TPM+1) matrix from T1S1, fit a limma linear model with the unpaired two-group design ~ condition (lesional vs control, using the exact labels from metadata.csv, control as reference so positive logFC = up in lesional), then eBayes with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE — the mean-variance trend on log-TPM is modelled by the trend option, which is what makes limma valid here in the absence of counts and precision weights. Report the full topTable for all tested genes: gene symbol, logFC (log2 TPM ratio), AveExpr, moderated t, raw p, BH-adjusted p (FDR), and B. caveats: GSEA on a ranking derived from log-TPM inherits the compositional caveat from T1S2 — a broad apparent down-shift may reflect TPM renormalization rather than coordinated repression

With 6 vs 6 samples, permutation should be over genes rather than sample labels; state which was used, since gene-permutation p-values are anti-conservative for correlated gene sets

The seed reference census confirms the staged human collections: MSigDB hallmark (h.all, 50 sets), MSigDB GO-BP (c5.go.bp, ~7,538 sets), and WikiPathways human — all symbol-based and human, matching this dataset's organism.
steps.question: Which biological processes and pathways are coordinately shifted in psoriasis lesional versus control skin, given the ranked lesional-vs-control statistic?
constraints: Use the human collections only — this is Homo sapiens skin; do not substitute the mouse hallmark file
Run the rank-based test on the full ranked list from T1S2, not on a thresholded list, as the primary analysis
Use the set of genes actually tested in T1S2 as the background universe for the over-representation secondary analysis, never the full genome
Resolve gene-set files from the environment's reference store at run time; do not hard-code assumptions about which collections exist
Report BH-adjusted p-values and NES; do not report raw permutation p-values as the decision statistic
steps.description: Take the ranked gene list from T1S2 (all tested genes ordered by the limma moderated t statistic) and run a rank-based gene set enrichment test (GSEA / fgsea-style, permutation-based, BH-corrected) against human gene-set collections resolved from the environment's reference store: the MSigDB human hallmark collection, the MSigDB human GO biological-process collection, and the human WikiPathways collection. All are keyed on HGNC gene symbols, which matches the first column of tpm.csv, so no ID conversion should be needed — report the fraction of ranked genes that map into each collection's universe and flag it if symbol overlap is poor (a sign of outdated or aliased symbols). Restrict sets to those with between 10 and 500 members present in the tested universe. Report, per collection, the significantly enriched sets (FDR < 0.05) with normalized enrichment score, direction, set size, leading-edge genes, and produce a dot plot of the top enriched sets by NES in each direction. The fraction of the ranked gene list that maps into each collection's gene universe is reported
Significant sets (FDR < 0.05) are tabulated per collection with NES, direction, size and leading-edge genes, and written to CSV
Redundant GO-BP terms are grouped by leading-edge overlap before a headline count is reported
A secondary over-representation test on the T1S2 significant gene set is run using the tested genes as background, and disagreements with the GSEA result are noted

plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control DE from TPM (limma-trend)
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a gene-level TPM matrix only (12,000 genes x 12 samples, /data/inputs/abundance/tpm.csv) with a 12-row metadata table giving condition; 6 lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. No raw counts and no Salmon quantification directories were delivered, so the count-based negative-binomial workflows (DESeq2, edgeR) are not applicable — they require integer counts and library-size offsets, and coercing TPM into them (rounding, 'pseudo-counts') fabricates a dispersion structure that does not exist and inflates significance. The defensible route on TPM is log2(TPM+1) with a Gaussian model: limma with trend=TRUE and robust empirical-Bayes moderation, which is the method limma's own authors recommend for log-CPM/log-TPM-like data and which handles the mean-variance trend without needing counts. Track 1 therefore does QC on the TPM matrix itself (library composition, detection rates, sample correlation, PCA, outlier and sample-swap check against the metadata labels) and then the lesional-vs-control contrast with BH FDR control, reporting effect sizes as log2 fold-changes of TPM. Because TPM is a within-sample compositional measure, a handful of extremely high-expressing genes (in psoriatic lesional skin: KRT6/16/17, S100A7/8/9, SERPINB3/4, DEFB4A) can compress every other gene's TPM in those samples; the QC step must quantify that compositional load and the DE step must be interpreted with it in mind, so a between-sample quantile/median normalization on the log scale is applied and reported explicitly. Track 2 takes the ranked statistic from the DE step into gene-set analysis against the staged human MSigDB hallmark and GO-BP collections and human WikiPathways, using a rank-based (GSEA/fgsea-style) test on the full ranked list rather than an over-representation test on a thresholded list, which is the more stable choice at n=6 per group. Positive-control expectation: psoriatic lesional skin should show strong IL-17/TNF-driven inflammation, keratinocyte hyperproliferation and antimicrobial peptide induction; absence of that signal is itself informative and would point at a labelling or quantification problem rather than a subtle biology. The whole analysis is small (a 12,000 x 13 CSV), so resource needs are modest throughout. Every deliverable carries the TPM caveat: these are moderated-t results on abundances, not counts, and are directionally reliable but their p-values are less well calibrated than a count-based model on the same experiment would be.
